podcast.title: Gottschalk - "Morte!" Performance and Death
podcast.body: Gottschalk's final performance saw him play a piece titled "Morte!" (Portuguese for death), before collapsing on stage and succumbing three weeks later to a quinine overdose. "Shortly after playing a piece called Morty with an exclamation mark, which is Portuguese for death."

podcast.title: Gottschalk - Civil War Exile
podcast.body: Louis Moreau Gottschalk was exiled from his Southern home for supporting the Union during the Civil War, and later left the United States to reside in South America. "He was first exiled from his home in the south due to his support for the north in the Civil War, and then later had to leave the US altogether and move to South America."

podcast.title: Gottschalk - Incorporator of Folk Melodies
podcast.body: Gottschalk integrated folk melodies he encountered in New Orleans into his compositions, drawing from a diverse range of influences present in the city's unique musical environment. "Gotshawk knew and incorporated folk melodies he heard in New Orleans."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 8: The Fat Man and Fats Domino

podcast.title: Gottschalk - Pioneer of New Orleans Music
podcast.body: Gottschalk's compositions sound remarkably modern, akin to music from the 1920s or 1930s, because he was the first to formalize New Orleans musical elements into a permanent written form. "Gotshawk was the first person to put New Orleans music into some sort of permanent form."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Gottschalk - Precursor to 20th Century Music Careers
podcast.body: Gottschalk's life and career foreshadowed those of many 20th-century musicians, with New Orleans continually revolutionizing popular music using techniques he had pioneered. "Gotshawk also presaged the careers of many 20th century musicians."

podcast.title: Gottschalk - Romantic Composer
podcast.body: Gottschalk exemplified the romantic archetype, composing pieces with evocative titles such as "The Dying Poet." "He wrote pieces called things like The Dying Poet."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Gottschalk - Scandal and Death
podcast.body: After a scandalous affair involving his students, Gottschalk contracted yellow fever and tragically collapsed on stage, never recovering. "After a scandalous affair with the students, he eventually contracted yellow fever and collapsed on stage."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Gottschalk - Virtuoso Pianist
podcast.body: Louis Moreau Gottschalk was widely considered the greatest pianist of his generation, recognized for his flashy showmanship and unique ability to manipulate the keyboard in ways others could not. "he was considered the greatest pianist of his generation, a flashy showman of the keyboard, who could make it do things no one else could."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Gottschalk's Contemporaries and Influences
podcast.body: Louis Moreau Gottschalk was known to Chopin and Liszt, and his influence extended to teaching someone who later played for Abraham Lincoln, highlighting his connection to significant figures of his era. "someone who knew Chopin and List, someone who was writing so long ago, he taught someone who played for Abraham Lincoln."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 8: The Fat Man and Fats Domino

podcast.title: Gottschalk's Posthumous Recognition - Composer vs. Performer
podcast.body: During his lifetime, Louis Moreau Gottschalk was dismissed as a romantic composer, mocked by figures like Mark Twain, and largely forgotten for decades after his early death, remembered primarily as an extraordinary pianist rather than a composer. "Mark Twain made fun of his style, and he was largely forgotten for decades after his early death."
